newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU calculations for Italy's 1997 budget deficit.
newsitem.headline: EU calculations for Italy's 1997 budget deficit.

text.p: The sum total of the European Union's recent rulings on Italy's 1997 budget plans would leave its deficit at 3.1 percent of gross domestic product, all things being equal.
The European Commission warned on Friday that it would be misleading to make such an extrapolation, given changes in Italy's underlying economic situation.
But following is a summary of what the EU executive had assumed in its autumn forecast for Italy and where things stand now, assuming no change in the economic outlook.
In November, the Commission anticipated Italy's 1997 budget deficit would come in at 3.3 percent of GDP.
This forecast took full account of the proposed euro-tax, worth approximately 0.6 percent of output.
In January, Eurostat, the EU's statistical office, ruled in favour of Italy's treatment of interest on postal bonds, an assumption the Commission did not incorporate into its autumn assessment.
The amount involved was worth 0.3 percent of GDP, so ahead of Friday's euro tax decision, the Commission's deficit estimate would have theoretically been brought down to 3.0 percent of GDP.
The last area of uncertainty, treatment of state guarantees to Italy's railway system, was judged acceptable on Friday, totalling 0.2 percent of output.
Commission officials on Friday said they had incorporated a deficit reduction of 0.3 percent of GDP in their November estimate for such guarantees.
